metaDescription: Clearview Acres sits near Rock Springs on Sweetwater County's checkerboard corridor. Get a courthouse-checked read on your mineral interest before selling.
heroLead: Clearview Acres sits close to Rock Springs, right in the middle of Sweetwater County's Union Pacific checkerboard corridor, where private and federal minerals alternate section by section.
intro: This whole stretch along the old transcontinental railroad grant was patterned into alternating odd and even sections back in the 1860s, odd sections going to the railroad and later into private hands, even sections staying federal. That pattern still governs mineral ownership here today, and it's the first thing I check before saying anything about a Clearview Acres tract.

Rock Springs and Green River have a long coal and trona mining history alongside oil and gas, so I also check whether your deed describes oil and gas minerals specifically, or something else entirely, before quoting a number.

sections.heading: Checkerboard ownership up close
paragraphs: If your family's interest traces to a Union Pacific land grant patent, you likely hold private minerals outright, sellable without any federal leasing process involved. If your legal description falls on an even, federally-retained section instead, there's no private interest there to sell, though you might hold private minerals on an adjacent or nearby odd section.
I confirm this section by section using the Sweetwater County recorder's records, not assumptions based on the neighborhood.

sections.heading: What's actually been developed nearby
paragraphs: Sweetwater County has seen tight-gas development in trends stretching from the Jonah and Pinedale area south toward Continental Divide-Creston. Clearview Acres itself sits closer to Rock Springs than to the most active drilling, so most interests here price as undeveloped rather than currently producing, unless your specific section shows otherwise.

Rock Springs' industrial base, coal, trona, and natural gas processing, has meant steady leasing interest in this corridor for decades, even where drilling itself hasn't followed through. That leasing history alone is worth documenting, even on acreage that's never seen a rig.

faqs.question: How do I check if my section is checkerboard private land?
faqs.answer: Send your legal description and I'll verify it against the county plat and original land grant records.

faqs.question: Do I own trona or coal rights instead of oil and gas?
faqs.answer: Depends on your deed language. I'll review it and tell you plainly which mineral rights you actually hold.

faqs.question: Is there active oil and gas leasing near Clearview Acres?
faqs.answer: I'll check current lease filings for your specific section before answering definitively.

faqs.question: What if my tract has been leased but never drilled?
faqs.answer: That's common here. I'll factor the lease history into pricing even without an actual wellbore on your section.
